messages:
Acme Support: Hey team — after the March 23 rollout our docs generator started returning malformed markdown. Several customers report code fences missing the closing ``` and in some cases a stray ellipsis token '...' ends up inside code blocks. Happening on rwd-text-v1 (variant v0.9.12). Ticket 98765.

Acme Support: Minimal example (we send via our integration):
```json
{
  "model": "rwd-text-v1",
  "input": "Generate docs for this snippet:
```python
print('hello')
```,
  "max_tokens": 60
}
```

Acme Support: Response we got (note missing closing fence and an extra token):
```text
```python
print('hello')
...

# no closing backticks here
```
```

Aisha Khan: @Acme Support thanks — can you paste the exact API call (curl or SDK) and confirm whether you are passing a `stop`/`stop_sequences` param? Also which region and whether you're on hosted or dedicated.

Acme Support: We call the hosted API in us-west1 via our connector. We don't explicitly set `stop_sequences`; we relied on the model to preserve fences. Here's the exact curl we used: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-text-v1","input":"```python
print(\'hello\')
```","max_tokens":60}'
```

support-bot: Created escalation INC-3421 and linked to ticket 98765 :rotating_light:

Tom Ortega: I pulled the same request against hosted us-west1 and I can reproduce locally. If I send the raw prompt (with fences) I sometimes see the trailing `...` token appended inside the block and the closing fence dropped. Repro steps below.

Tom Ortega: Repro snippet (python SDK):
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=\"sk-XXX\")
resp = client.generate(model=\"rwd-text-v1\", input='''```python
print(\'hello\')
```''', max_tokens=60)
print(resp.text)
```

Tom Ortega: Example bad output I got: "```python
print('hello')
...
" — no closing backticks. I've reproduced 7/20 times in a short loop. :eyes:

Lena Park: Noted. We shipped a runtime patch in yesterday's rollout (deploy id: deploy-2026-03-23T03:12Z) that changed token-level stop handling to use a faster kernel. Canary showed perf wins but we disabled legacy stop-trimming. Possible that the new path mishandles sequences that include punctuation + backticks.

deploy-bot: Deployed service/infra rwd-runtime@v1.14.0 to canary (canary_id=canary-17), rollout window 2026-03-23T03:12Z. Config diff: `stop_sequence_handling=fast` (previous `legacy`).

Lena Park: I'm going to grab model logs for canary-17 and check the tokenizer outputs and post-cache KV. Tom, can you attach a full request/response pair (raw bytes) for one reproducible example? That helps trace token ids.

Tom Ortega: Pasted raw JSON of the failing response in INC-3421. Observed token ids end with [5021, 6, 11] where 11 corresponds to '.' token in the sentencepiece vocab; then runtime emitted EOF without appending fence tokens.

Aisha Khan: For a quick mitigation, request-level workaround we can suggest to customers: explicitly set `stop_sequences` to include the fence string (e.g., "```"), or post-process to append a closing fence if the last line starts with code indentation. But setting `stop_sequences` may still be affected if runtime mis-trims.

Tom Ortega: I tested setting `stop_sequences=["```"]` — that prevents the `...` in some runs but sometimes the fence still gets lost. Looks like the issue is at the kernel-level trimming that decides when to terminate and whether to emit the literal fence.

Lena Park: Ok, immediate plan: 1) Rollback the `stop_sequence_handling=fast` change from canary to prevent wider impact while we root-cause. 2) Eng-runtime will add an extra unit test that includes fenced markdown and ellipsis/punctuation edge cases. 3) Eng-ml to review tokenizer change (commit ab12f3c) that was landed 2026-03-22. 4) Support to notify affected customers with a recommended workaround (explicit stop + post-process).

deploy-bot: Initiating canary rollback for canary-17 -> target config `stop_sequence_handling=legacy`.

Lena Park: I deployed the rollback to canary-17; monitoring tail logs now. If canary looks stable we'll promote. Can anyone run a quick smoke against the canary endpoint?

Tom Ortega: Running smoke now against canary endpoint. Re-ran the 100-loop test. I no longer reproduce the missing fence or `...` artifacts in 100 trials. Looks good on my side.

Aisha Khan: Great. Action items: 
- eng-runtime (Lena) to finish root-cause writeup and open PR to reintroduce fast path with correct trimming tests (ETA 48h).
- eng-ml (assign) to confirm tokenizer vectors and add regression test (ETA 24h).
- support (Tom/Aisha) to send a status update to INC-3421 and affected customers with workaround and ETA.

Aisha Khan: Draft message to customers: "We rolled back a runtime change that affected stop-sequence handling. Workaround: include explicit `stop_sequences` in your request or run a trivial post-processing pass that ensures code fences are closed. We're working on a fix and will follow up asap."

Acme Support: Thanks for the quick triage and rollback. We'll validate on our side and reopen the ticket if anything else pops up.

support-bot: INC-3421 updated: status=investigating -> mitigated; note=canary rollback applied; monitor=72h.
